links.comparator_used: Pre-implementation period (18 months before the CoMET risk score display), with no risk score display
links.outcome: Incidence of PICU cardiac arrest events per 1000 patient days, and arrests with versus without return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC)
links.effect: Overall arrest rate fell from 3.0 (95% CI 2.0-4.4) to 2.4 (95% CI 1.6-3.5) per 1000 patient days, a non-significant decrease. Arrests without ROSC fell from 1.4 (95% CI 0.7-2.4) to 0.4 (95% CI 0.1-0.9) per 1000 patient days (incidence rate difference 1.0, 95% CI 0.13-1.8), about 7 fewer per year. Arrests with ROSC rose 50% (p = 0.025). Case fatality (42.5%) and ECLS use did not differ between periods.
links.tradeoff: Alert burden and protocol adherence were not measured. One or both scores exceeded 4 about 4.7% of the time, roughly 21 instances per day. The design was a single-centre, unadjusted pre-post comparison.
links.quote: The cardiac arrest incidence rate dropped from 3.0 events per 1000 patient days (95% CI 2.0–4.4) in the pre-CoMET period to 2.4 events per 1000 patient days (95% CI 1.6–3.5) in the post-CoMET period ( Fig. 2 ).

design_hint: Real-time display of risk scores on ICU monitors (pre/post implementation)
